chunks: My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abdillah from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man testifies against another man regarding disbelief, one of two cases will occur: if he testifies against a disbeliever, his testimony is true; but if he testifies against a believer, the disbelief returns to him. And beware of striking/slandering the believers.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who testifies to the disbelief of a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the theological risk of *takfir* (declaring disbelief), establishing a binary outcome where the accuser either validates the truth or incurs the very disbelief they accused. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on caution in judging others' faith, warning that false testimony against a believer results in the accuser's own spiritual ruin. The narration serves as a practical guide for maintaining communal harmony by avoiding baseless accusations among the faithful.
